subject: Invoice submission webhooks — PO correlation fields & acceptance guide
messages:
From: Leah Morgan <leah@stratospay.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: accounting@stratospay.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Invoice webhook + PO correlation — onboarding question

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. Our AP team (cc’d) wants to push invoice submissions into our system via a webhook rather than SFTP. Before we proceed we need to confirm the exact fields Redwood will send so we can map them to our PO engine. Key asks from accounting: 

- Confirm field(s) used to correlate to a customer PO (PO number, PO line reference, external_reference_id, etc.)
- Ability to include multiple PO numbers on a single invoice (some invoices will apply to 2+ POs)
- Support for invoice-level and line-level VAT/Tax breakdowns (country code + rate)
- A reliable request header or signature we can use to verify authenticity (preferred HMAC-SHA256)
- Retry semantics / idempotency key behavior (what should we do on 409/500)

Can you send the payload spec and a short acceptance checklist so our integration team can sign off? We’d like to stand up a test endpoint by end of week.

Thanks,
Leah Morgan
Finance Systems Manager
StratosPay

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>
To: Leah Morgan <leah@stratospay.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Invoice webhook + PO correlation — onboarding question

Leah — great questions. Putting answers and a minimal acceptance checklist below. I’ve attached our formal spec (redwood-ap-webhook-spec-v1.pdf) and a sample JSON payload (sample-invoice-payload.json) to accelerate mapping.

Summary answers (short):
- PO correlation: we send invoice.headers.po_numbers (array of strings) and invoice.lines[].po_number (optional per-line). Primary matching field is invoice.headers.po_numbers[0] when present; if missing we fall back to invoice.headers.external_reference_id.
- Multiple POs: supported. invoice.headers.po_numbers is an ordered array — we preserve order coming from the UI/system.
- VAT/tax: invoice.lines[].tax { country_code, rate_percent, tax_amount } and invoice.totals.tax_breakdown (array) at invoice level.
- Auth: HMAC-SHA256 using X-Redwood-Signature header (hex). We rotate keys per customer — we will provide test key for your staging endpoint.
- Idempotency: each webhook includes X-Redwood-Event-Id (uuid) and invoice.headers.idempotency_key when present. We retry with exponential backoff for 5 attempts; final state after retries will be POSTed to your /webhook/receipt endpoint with header X-Redwood-Retry: n. On 409 you should treat as duplicate and return 200 if content matches.

Acceptance checklist (minimal):
1) Test endpoint reachable over HTTPS (TLS 1.2+).
2) Staging HMAC key configured and verified by you (we’ll provide test key).
3) Mapping created for invoice.headers.po_numbers (array) -> AP system PO lookup field(s).
4) Line-level tax fields mapped and mapped sums reconciled to invoice.totals.total_tax.
5) Idempotency / duplicate-handling behavior validated using sample-invoice-payload.json (attached).
6) Verify handling of multi-PO invoices (we’ll send a synthetic test with 2 POs).

Next steps: please share a staging endpoint URL and whether you want JSON Schema or an OpenAPI webhook consumer contract (we can provide both). I’ll ask Jordan to chime in on SLA/exceptions for queued deliveries.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-ap-webhook-spec-v1.pdf, sample-invoice-payload.json

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 13:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Invoice webhook + PO correlation — onboarding question

Leah — quick note from a routing / SLA perspective:

- Default delivery SLO: attempts every 30s, then 1m, 2m, 5m, 10m (5 attempts total). We can extend attempts for enterprise agreements.
- For customers with strict AP windows we support a hold-and-bulk mode: Redwood will queue invoices and POST a single bulk payload at a scheduled time (e.g., 06:00 UTC daily) — useful when you want a nightly handshake.
- Exceptions: If your endpoint returns 422 we will surface the payload and error to your console and mark the webhook as “requires manual review” — we do not auto-delete.

If StratosPay needs a signed delivery guarantee or SFTP as fallback for failures beyond retries, we can enable an SFTP fallback workflow (additional setup and costs).

Jordan Blake
Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

Cc: Vivek — can you confirm the HMAC header name and length?

Thanks Stephanie and Jordan — that covers the majority of it. A couple quick confirmations before we schedule the test: 

- We’ll stand up https://staging-ap.stratospay.com/webhook/redwood and will share TLS cert details and the endpoint this afternoon.
- Please send the staging HMAC key and the JSON Schema (both preferred). Once we validate signatures we’ll run the sample-invoice-payload through our mapping and report exceptions.
- For multi-PO invoices we’ll accept the array and attempt to match to multiple POs; if a PO cannot be found we’ll return 422 with a body of { "missing_po": "<po_number>" } and expect Redwood to flag it in the console.

We prefer the nightly bulk POST for large volumes — can you include instructions for switching between real-time vs scheduled bulk in the spec?

I’ll loop in our Integration Lead (accounting@stratospay.com) on the endpoint details. Look forward to the sample key and schema.

Best,
Leah
